hook.en: A family of four sets out to sail around the world, following the route of a famous explorer. They have prepared for years. Will it be enough?

objectives.en: Introduce the authors and the true-life account
Identify the family and the crew of Wavewalker
Explain the aim and route of the voyage

narration.en: A family of four sets out to sail around the world, following the route of a famous explorer. They have prepared for years. Will it be enough?

body.en: This is a true adventure narrative by Gordon Cook and Alan East, told in the first person by the father of the family. In July 1976 he, his wife Mary, their six-year-old son Jonathan and seven-year-old daughter Suzanne set sail from Plymouth, England. They hoped to repeat the round-the-world voyage made two hundred years earlier by the explorer Captain James Cook.

points.en: Authors: Gordon Cook and Alan East
Narrator: the father, an experienced sailor
Aim: retrace Captain James Cook's voyage

explanation.en: The family set sail from Plymouth in July 1976; two crewmen joined for the rough southern Indian Ocean.

caption.en: Trace the route: Plymouth in England, south to Cape Town, then east across the southern Indian Ocean towards Ile Amsterdam.

narration.en: Turn the globe. Find England, follow the Atlantic down to the tip of Africa, then move east into the wide, empty southern Indian Ocean. That is where the storm struck.

body.en: The narrator and Mary had spent many years sharpening their sailing skills, and they spent months preparing their boat, Wavewalker, a sturdy wooden-hulled vessel, and testing her in rough weather. The first leg, from England to Cape Town, passed smoothly. At Cape Town two crewmen joined them to help with one of the roughest seas in the world, the southern Indian Ocean: Larry Vigil, an American, and Herb Seigler, a Swiss.

points.en: Boat: Wavewalker, professionally built and well tested
First leg to Cape Town: no trouble
Crew added: Larry Vigil (American), Herb Seigler (Swiss)
Next: the stormy southern Indian Ocean

problem.en: Why did the narrator take on two crewmen at Cape Town?

steps.en: The next leg crossed the southern Indian Ocean.
It is one of the roughest seas in the world.
Extra hands would help sail and repair the boat in storms.

answer.en: After Cape Town the family had to cross the southern Indian Ocean, one of the roughest seas in the world. The narrator took on two experienced crewmen, Larry Vigil and Herb Seigler, to help handle the boat in the storms ahead.
